policy: End consumer carbon price (federal fuel charge set to zero)
legislative_vehicle: Order in council (fuel charge to $0 from 2025-04-01); statutory repeal of GGPPA Part 1 in Bill C-4 Part 3
stated_target_or_metric: Govt claim: cut gas prices ~18 cents/L in most provinces; final Canada Carbon Rebate April 2025; C-31 ends rebate payments for returns filed after 2026-10-30
notes: Industrial (output-based) carbon pricing retained. Order-in-council date from media (CBC 2025-03-14); statutory repeal confirmed in C-4 royal-assent text. C-31 (Budget 2025 Implementation Act No.2) still in committee.

policy: Cancel proposed capital gains inclusion-rate increase (1/2 to 2/3)
legislative_vehicle: None needed (2024 proposal was never enacted); LCGE increase to $1.25M legislated in C-15
outcome_indicators: n/a (revenue effect noted in Budget 2025 revenue outlook)
notes: Budget 2025 cites the cancellation as a reason corporate and personal income tax revenue growth is soft in 2025-26.

policy: Middle-class tax cut: lowest federal PIT rate 15% -> 14% (14.5% for 2025, 14% from 2026)
legislative_vehicle: Bill C-4 Part 1 (Making Life More Affordable for Canadians Act)
stated_target_or_metric: Govt: 22 million people; up to $840/yr for a two-income family. PBO: net cost $28.2B over 2025-26 to 2029-30; avg saving $110 (2025-26) to $200 (2029-30) per filer
notes: Applied via payroll from July 2025 ahead of royal assent (normal ways-and-means practice). PBO: ~39,000 filers (AMT / high non-refundable credits) pay slightly more in 2026. C-15 added a temporary credit addressing that issue (item z.3).

policy: Rescind Digital Services Tax
legislative_vehicle: Bill C-15 Part 2 (repeals Digital Services Tax Act)
notes: Announced after the US suspended trade talks; repeal retroactive to the Act (refunds with interest per Finance letter of 2025-09-13).

policy: Eliminate Underused Housing Tax (2025 and later years)
End luxury tax on aircraft and vessels (cars over $100k still taxed)
Productivity Super-Deduction (reinstated Accelerated Investment Incentive, immediate expensing for M&P buildings, productivity-enhancing assets, SR&ED capex, clean energy, ZEVs)
legislative_vehicle: Bill C-15 (most items); C-31 (immediate expensing of M&P buildings, still in committee)
stated_target_or_metric: Govt: lowers Canada's marginal effective tax rate (METR) by more than 2 points; lowest METR in G7. PBO: cost $19.4B over 5 yrs (mostly timing/deferral)
notes: Too early for investment response; business M&E investment fell through 2025 and rebounded in 2026Q2 (tariff, oil-price and uncertainty effects dominate).

policy: SR&ED enhancements (higher expenditure limit for 35% credit, eligibility for public corporations)
Temporary suspension of federal fuel excise tax (gasoline 10c/L, diesel 4c/L)
legislative_vehicle: Bill C-30 Part 2 (Apr 20 - Sep 7, 2026); extension in Bill C-38 to 2027-01-31 then 50% to 2027-03-31
stated_target_or_metric: PBO: $4.9B in 2026-27 for both phases; ~$276 per family
notes: Response to 2026 Middle East oil shock. Extension (announced 2026-09-02) is at report stage in the House as of 2026-10-10; C-38 deems it in force from 2026-09-08.

policy: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (top-up to GST credit)
stated_target_or_metric: Govt: >12 million people; up to $1,890 this year for a family of four

policy: Reduce CPP contribution rate from 2027
notes: Too early.

policy: Build Canada Homes (federal agency/Crown corp to build non-market and affordable housing; $13B initial capitalization)
legislative_vehicle: Funding: Bill C-15 Part 5 Div 3 (up to $11.5B + $1.515B to Canada Lands); Crown corporation: Bill C-20 (Build Canada Homes Act)
stated_target_or_metric: Govt: part of national effort to "double the pace of housing construction over the next decade" (campaign: nearly 500,000 homes/yr). PBO: BCH adds ~26,000 units over 5 yrs (+2.1% vs baseline completions; 3.7% of 690,000-unit 2035 gap)
notes: SEU 2026 dropped explicit pace targets (PBO NT-2627-003). PBO: total federal housing program spending falls 56% from $9.8B (2025-26) to $4.3B (2028-29).

policy: GST rebate for first-time buyers on new homes (100% up to $1M; phased out $1M-$1.5M)
stated_target_or_metric: Govt: saves up to $50,000. PBO cost: $1.9B over 6 years
notes: No public take-up data found.

policy: Development-charge reductions via federal-provincial deals ($1.7B to provinces/territories; e.g. Ontario cuts DCs up to 50% for 3 years)
legislative_vehicle: Bill C-26 (payments out of CRF to improve housing supply)
stated_target_or_metric: Jurisdictions with highest DCs required to cut them for 3 years
notes: Too early for supply effects.

policy: One Canadian Economy Act (Bill C-5): Free Trade and Labour Mobility in Canada Act + Building Canada Act
stated_target_or_metric: Remove federal barriers to internal trade; fast-track "national interest projects" (Schedule 1 of Building Canada Act)
outcome_indicators: No post-2025 interprovincial trade data yet (StatCan annual interprovincial trade lags ~2 yrs)
notes: As of the Justice Laws consolidation current to 2026-09-21, Schedule 1 (national interest projects) is EMPTY. Gazette notices of intent (30-day) published for West Coast Oil Pipeline (2026-08-01), Mackenzie Valley Highway and Roberts Bank Terminal 2 (2026-08-29, per secondary source), and Deep Geological Repository (2026-09-19). Bill C-39 (Sept 2026) would amend the Building Canada Act and Impact Assessment Act.

policy: Major Projects Office (MPO) and referred "nation-building" projects
legislative_vehicle: Administrative (Privy Council Office); designation power under Building Canada Act
stated_target_or_metric: Govt (SEU 2026): 15 projects referred, >$125B capital, >60,000 construction jobs
notes: Referral to MPO is not the same as designation under the Building Canada Act (none designated as of 2026-09-21).

policy: Remove federal exceptions to the Canadian Free Trade Agreement; mutual recognition of goods; labour mobility service standard
stated_target_or_metric: Govt: all 53 federal CFTA exceptions removed by June 2025; FPT agreement to sign Canadian Mutual Recognition Agreement on Sale of Goods; IMF: removing internal frictions could lift real GDP by up to ~7% over time
notes: Provincial barriers (the bulk) depend on provinces.

policy: Reach NATO 2% of GDP in 2025-26 (~$9B additional)
legislative_vehicle: Supplementary Estimates (A) 2025-26 / Appropriation Acts; Budget 2025 ($81.8B over 5 yrs)
notes: NATO measures on a cash, calendar-year basis; federal accounts are accrual, fiscal-year.

policy: NATO Hague commitment: 5% of GDP by 2035 (3.5% core + up to 1.5% ancillary); Canada interim 4% total (2.5% core) by 2030
legislative_vehicle: Political commitment; Defence Investment Agency (announced 2025-10-02); Bill C-40 (defence procurement, introduced 2026-10-06)
stated_target_or_metric: 3.5% core by 2035; PBO: requires ~$33.5B/yr extra cash on average; core spending ~$159-164B in 2035-36; +$63B deficit and +6.3 pts debt/GDP in 2035-36
notes: No published federal spending path to 5% (PBO).

policy: Budget 2025: capital vs operating budget framework; anchors = balance operating budget by 2028-29 and declining deficit-to-GDP
legislative_vehicle: Budget 2025 (tabled); implementation Acts C-15 (RA 2026-03-26), C-31 (in committee)
notes: PBO: govt definition of capital is "overly expansive" (~$94B or 30% larger than PBO definition over 2024-25 to 2029-30); 7.5% chance deficit/GDP falls every year; IMF recommends debt anchor.

policy: Comprehensive Expenditure Review: $60B savings+revenues over 5 yrs; ~$13B/yr by 2028-29; public service down ~40,000 positions (~10%) by 2028-29 vs 2023-24
legislative_vehicle: Budget 2025; C-15 Divs 6-7 (early retirement options for workforce reduction)
outcome_indicators: PBO Federal Employment Tracking Tool: FTEs 367k peak (Jun 2024) -> 342k (Jun 2026); FY avg 358k (2024-25) -> 344k (2025-26)
notes: Positions vs FTEs are not identical concepts; decline began before Budget 2025 (from mid-2024).

policy: 2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan: PR 380,000/yr; new temporary resident arrivals 385,000 (2026), 370,000 (2027-28) vs 673,650 in 2025; NPRs < 5% of population by end-2027
legislative_vehicle: Levels Plan (administrative); C-12 (Strengthening Canada's Immigration System and Borders Act, RA 2026-03-26)
stated_target_or_metric: NPR share < 5% by end of 2027; PR < 1% of population beyond 2027
notes: TR reductions began under the previous government (2024 caps, 2025-2027 plan). PBO projects NPR share just under 5% by end-2027 and ~flat population in 2026.

policy: Counter-tariffs on US goods (25% on ~$30B from 2025-03-04; on ~$29.8B steel/aluminum/other from 2025-03-13; autos from 2025-04-09)
legislative_vehicle: Orders under Customs Tariff (United States Surtax Order 2025 etc.); remission order 2025-04-16
notes: Budget 2025: $6.7B gross revenue assessed to 2025-10-17, $3.0B remitted, net $3.7B. First measures predate Carney (sworn in 2025-03-14).

policy: Removal of most counter-tariffs on US goods (kept steel, aluminum, autos)
New counter-tariffs after Canada-US talks broke down: 15/25/50% surtaxes on $27.6B of US goods + $7.5B support package
legislative_vehicle: United States Surtax Order (2026) (per secondary sources); CBSA notice
stated_target_or_metric: Mirror US 50% tariff on $27.6B of Canadian goods effective 2026-08-22
outcome_indicators: too early (Sept 2026 trade data not yet released)
notes: Support package on top of ~$25B earlier tariff supports.

policy: Buy Canadian procurement policy
stated_target_or_metric: Federal departments and Crown corps (e.g. BCH) to prefer Canadian suppliers
notes: Effective date from media (CTV).

policy: Double non-US exports (goods and services) over the next decade (+$300B); $6B Trade Infrastructure Strategy incl. $5B Trade Diversification Corridors Fund
notes: Govt: non-US goods+services exports +$33B in 2025 vs 2024. Goods-only StatCan data show non-US share rising; much of the rise is gold (UK) and crude oil (price effects, TMX opened May 2024).

policy: Canada-Indonesia CEPA
UK accession to CPTPP (implementation)
Canada-China strategic partnership (China to reduce/suspend tariffs on key agri-food and seafood); other FTA talks (India by end-2026, UAE, ASEAN, Philippines, Mercosur)
notes: Details of China arrangement not verified from primary text.

policy: Consumer-Driven Banking Act (open banking) re-enacted
Ban most non-compete clauses (federally regulated employers)
notes: C-31 at committee in House as of 2026-10-10.

policy: Competition Act: remove internationally-recognized-methodology requirement for environmental claims (greenwashing provisions)
Red Tape Reduction Act amendments (temporary regulatory exemptions/sandboxes)
Building Canada Strong Act (Impact Assessment Act, Building Canada Act, CER Act, Fisheries Act, Canada Marine Act amendments; Enabling Digital Trade Act)
notes: At committee in House as of 2026-10-10.

policy: High-Speed Rail Network Act (Alto, Quebec-Ontario)
notes: PBO cost analysis RP-2627-009-C (2026-10-01).

policy: Canada-Alberta MOU: support for a West Coast bitumen pipeline; proposed oil & gas emissions cap dropped; stronger industrial carbon price (TIER) and Pathways CCS
legislative_vehicle: MOU (non-legislative); Building Canada Act Gazette notice for West Coast Oil Pipeline (2026-08-01)
